Now we are merging two PDDL domains into one domain. Please help judge whether two PDDL operators are equivalent.

domain_1:
    action in domain_1: (:action sew_eggs :parameters (?t - entity) :precondition (and (is_tailor ?t) (has ?t needle) (eggs_shot brother_hunter)) :effect (eggs_sewn ?t))
    predicates explaination in domain_1: {'(eggs_sewn ?e - entity)': "entity ?e is in the state 'eggs sewn'; used as effect of sew_eggs, precondition of return_eggs_to_nest", '(eggs_shot ?e - entity)': "entity ?e is in the state 'eggs shot'; used as effect of shoot_eggs, precondition of sew_eggs", '(has ?e - entity ?i - item)': "relation 'has' holds; arguments: ?e is a entity, ?i is a item; used as effect of separate_at_crossroads, effect of learn_astronomer_trade, effect of learn_hunter_trade, effect of learn_tailor_trade, precondition of count_eggs, effect of count_eggs, effect of fetch_eggs, precondition of shoot_eggs", '(is_tailor ?e - entity)': "entity ?e is in the state 'is tailor'; used as effect of learn_tailor_trade, precondition of sew_eggs, precondition of repair_ship"}

domain_2:
    action in domain_2: (:action follow_pebbles_home :parameters (?g ?h - entity ?home ?path_loc - location) :precondition (and (pebble_on_path ?path_loc) (at ?h ?path_loc) (at ?g ?path_loc)) :effect (and (at ?h ?home) (at ?g ?home) (not (at ?h ?path_loc)) (not (at ?g ?path_loc)) (not (lost ?h)) (not (lost ?g))))
    predicates explaination in domain_2: {'(at ?e - entity ?l - location)': "relation 'at' holds; arguments: ?e is a entity, ?l is a location; used as effect of abandon_children_in_forest, precondition of leave_children_at_fire, precondition of drop_pebble_on_path, precondition of follow_pebbles_home, effect of follow_pebbles_home, precondition of drop_breadcrumb_on_path, precondition of follow_breadcrumbs_home, effect of follow_breadcrumbs_home", '(lost ?c - entity)': "entity ?c is in the state 'lost'; used as effect of abandon_children_in_forest, effect of leave_children_at_fire, effect of follow_pebbles_home, effect of follow_breadcrumbs_home, effect of wander_forest_seeking_way_out, effect of return_home_and_reunite_with_father", '(pebble_on_path ?l - location)': "location ?l is in the state 'pebble on path'; used as effect of drop_pebble_on_path, precondition of follow_pebbles_home"}

Please judge whether the two operators can be merged into one action based on following rules:
(1) If the two actions have the same name, they MUST be merged into one action;
(2) If the two actions are semantically equivalent (although they may differ in preconditions and effects), merge them. Genrally, you need to union their preconditions and effects.
(3) Note that do NOT merge two actions if the logic becomes more complex after merging. For example, do NOT use "or", "when" to union two actions (about their preconditions and effects). Namely NOT too general. 
(4) Do NOT invent any predicate.
(5) If you decide to merge two actions. You can invent new action name. But the new name must be reasonable according to the whole predicates in the action.
    For example: if the action expresses the meaning of "pick some object from drawer" according to the predicates in preconditions and effects, just name it like "pick_from_drawer", instead of "pick_from_container", etc.
(6) Keep the given PDDL style. Please use PDDL 1.0 and do NOT use Conditional Effects like "when", etc.
(7) Note the number of brackets in the PDDL format.

Your output should include four part:
(1) reasoning: your analysis process;
(2) merge_flag: whether the two operators can be merged into one;
(3) new_operator_name: if equivalent, output the new operator name (in one of the given operator or a new invented operator).
(4) new_operator: if equivalent, output the new operator in PDDL format.

If "merge_flag" is false, the "new_operator_name" and "new_operator" parts are null.

Your output should be in JSON format like below:
{
    "reasoning": "your analysis process",
    "merge_flag": true,
    "new_operator_name": "open_door",
    "new_operator": "(:action open_door \n :parameters (?r ?d) \n :precondition (and (hand_free ?r)) \n :effect (and (is_open ?d)))"
}

Do NOT output any strange symbols like "\".

The preconditions and effects of `follow_pebbles_home` involve `at`, `pebble_on_path`, and `lost`, which are related to the location of entities. The action `sew_eggs` involves `is_tailor`, `has`, and `eggs_shot`, which are related to the preparation of eggs. There is no direct semantic similarity between the two actions.
